name: Silt — Found-Object Street Installation Scene
description: Silt practitioners build large-scale temporary installations from Shelf debris — broken aug components, cracked housing materials, discarded corporate packaging, salvaged industrial parts — arranged in public spaces without permission and without announcement. The work appears overnight and is usually dismantled within days by the city or by the artists themselves. Silt's aesthetic philosophy, articulated in a spoken-word tradition rather than written manifestos, holds that Shelf refuse made visible is the only honest portrait of the city. Installations are called 'deposits' and their creators 'sediment' — individual identity is subsumed into the collective flow of material.
cultural_impact: Silt installations have twice blocked major Tier 2 transit arteries, generating significant media coverage and corporate complaints. Their material salvage practice has created informal supply relationships with Shelf waste-pickers, providing small supplemental income to some of the city's most economically marginal residents.
locations: Silt Yard (informal material storage, Shelf East)
The Deposit Site (rotating, usually announced 12 hours prior via Underworld boards)
story_hooks: A major Silt deposit incorporates what appears to be classified corporate hardware — the artists didn't know what they had, but now a corporate security team wants it back.
The city offers Silt a sanctioned installation space in exchange for stopping unauthorized work — the community must decide if legitimacy is worth the loss of transgression.
An elder Silt practitioner is dying and wants their body incorporated into a final deposit — the community is divided over whether this is a profound statement or a step too far.
